card.title: Cover Story Logistics
card.instruction: Accept that a secret plan exists, then focus on schedules, witnesses, explanations, cleanup, and what everyone must remember.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For Mum's surprise party, we're saying you brought the cake on the nine o'clock bus?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. She'll ask why she didn't see my car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The last bus leaves at eight. Can you claim you walked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She drove past me at half eight. I was empty-handed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the cake was already here. We need Dad to remember accepting it before his nap.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 tests the cake cover story, A3 checks it against the last bus, and A5 repairs the timeline by assigning Dad the earlier receipt.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's missing-car explanation supplies the transport problem A3 checks; B4's empty-handed sighting makes A5 move the cake delivery earlier.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains why a bus story is being used and B4 supplies a concrete witness that rules out the walk-with-cake version.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's sighting to make a different delivery time and recipient part of the shared account.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes Mum's surprise party and a proposed nine-o'clock cake arrival.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's Dad-before-nap detail gives the new cover an actionable corroborator rather than a detached comic line.
